summary: Security review of CC-0116 (per-ControlPlane Keystone DB credential scoping). All security-focus invariants hold. Per-tenant isolation is sound: dbCredentialRemoteKeyFor (reconcile_dbcredentials.go:37-39) embeds both {ns}/{name} so two ControlPlanes can never resolve to the same OpenBao DB-credential object; dbCredentialSecretName is name-only but the Secret/ExternalSecret lives in childNamespace(cp)=cp.Namespace (reconcile_infrastructure.go:44), so same-named CPs in different namespaces remain distinct namespace-scoped objects (the OpenBao remote key, the real shared-backend blast radius, always carries both axes). OpenBao policy changes are comment-only with no capability widening: eso-management.hcl keeps kv-v2/data/openstack/keystone/* read-only, eso-control-plane.hcl adds only a comment, the bootstrap seed at kv-v2/openstack/keystone/${cp_ns}/${cp_name}/db is deliberately NOT mark_eso_managed (read-only), and push-keystone-keys.hcl is unchanged and grants write only to fernet-keys/credential-keys (no .../db write). Secrets are never passed as cleartext CLI args nor logged: production bootstrap uses the in-pod @generate marker expanding to `bao write -field=random_bytes sys/tools/random/32` (write-bootstrap-secrets.sh:67-68), and reconcile_dbcredentials.go logs only Secret names and error strings (never secret values). The Owns(&esov1.ExternalSecret{}) watch (controlplane_controller.go:293) is CORRECT and not a dead watch: the operator creates the ExternalSecret and sets a controller owner reference of kind=ControlPlane (SetControllerReference at reconcile_dbcredentials.go:128), unlike ESO-materialised Secrets which carry ownerRef.kind=ExternalSecret and are handled via the separate field-indexer Watches(&Secret{}) mapper. No hardcoded production credentials; the condition-type const and Secret-name-suffix const both carry //nolint:gosec G101 false-positive markers (controlplane_controller.go:49, reconcile_dbcredentials.go:29). Managed mode correctly overrides keystone.Spec.Database.SecretRef to the operator-owned Secret only when ClusterRef != nil; brownfield is a true no-op leaving the user secretRef untouched (reconcile_keystone.go:118-121). No security issues found.

This is acceptable for a test fixture (no production credential, ephemeral backend, mirrors the existing multi-controlplane chainsaw seed pattern) but for defence-in-depth consistency with write-bootstrap-secrets.sh you could seed via an in-pod `bao write -field=random_bytes` generation so no cleartext appears in the kubectl-exec arg/process list even in CI logs. LOW / informational only — not a blocker.
